targets.approach: From Pincher Creek drive west on Highway 507 and follow township and range roads to a parking spot by the fence next to the natural-gas pump house beside Mill Creek. Hike south on the trails that follow Mill Creek to the Gladstone valley, cross the creek, and follow the valley trail upstream, watching for cairns where it drops into the creek bed, to Adams Lake below the wall (the camp is on the far side of the lake from where the trail arrives). Look for it above a big cone of scree, well off to the right of Mud Falcon Crack.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the route down its own anchors.
targets.name: Wonderous Wanderer

targets.approach: South of Jasper, take the Icefields Parkway side road (Highway 93A) past Athabasca Falls to Leech Lake and park at the pullout. A maintained trail leads through forest to the Lost Boys crag. The Aspen Beauty sector comes early as the trail runs beneath the cliff, just beyond the big boulder at its foot. Baby Feet starts a few metres right of Little Girly Man, at a short dark dihedral.
targets.name: baby feet

targets.approach: South of Jasper, take the Icefields Parkway side road (Highway 93A) past Athabasca Falls to Leech Lake and park at the pullout. A maintained trail leads through forest to the Lost Boys crag. Keep walking along the cliff base past the first short bolted routes to the sector where the routes become clean and tall with large rocks at their feet. The route starts just right of a low black streak and just left of a blackened boulder, working through small roofs in a faint left-facing corner before a larger roof near the top.
targets.name: Hillbillies Gone Straight

targets.approach: Park at the pullout with a garbage bin on Highway 16 between Hinton and Jasper and follow the main Cinquefoil hiking trail from the back of the lot. When the crag comes into view, take the right-hand branch at the faint fork before a rolling hill, then zigzag uphill and traverse a meadow to reach the foot of the wall. For the Cinquefoil Right sector, head right once at the wall. Fifth Gear shares its start with Starfish: clip Starfish's first bolt, then step left onto the middle bolt line.
targets.name: Fifth Gear

targets.approach: Park at the large pullout with an outhouse on Highway 16 northeast of Jasper, toward Hinton. The trail starts at the far end of the pullout from the outhouse: skirt the pond, climb the steep hill, and continue up and left along the obvious trail, bearing left at forks, past a ladder to the cliffs. Crescent Wall is a small wall of bolted routes with a set of top-rope routes reached by a walk-up scramble to the right; the approach has steep sections and ladders.
targets.name: Crescent Moon

targets.approach: Park at the large pullout with an outhouse on Highway 16 northeast of Jasper, toward Hinton. The trail starts at the far end of the pullout from the outhouse: skirt the pond, climb the steep hill, and continue up and left along the obvious trail, bearing left at forks, past a ladder to the cliffs. Crescent Wall is a small wall of bolted routes with a set of top-rope routes reached by a walk-up scramble to the right; the approach has steep sections and ladders. Slopers is reached by an easy scramble to its bolted anchors.
targets.name: Slopers

targets.approach: Drive the Mount Edith Cavell road, which leaves the Icefields Parkway south of Jasper, to its end at the parking lot. Dune Wall is a conspicuous rock buttress at the foot of Mount Sorrow, to the right of Angel Glacier. Ford the creek and work up scree and stunted firs to the foot of the cliff. The route follows a left-facing corner reached past a ledge with a tree.
targets.name: Bodhisatva

targets.approach: Drive the Mount Edith Cavell road, which leaves the Icefields Parkway south of Jasper, to its end at the parking lot. Dune Wall is a conspicuous rock buttress at the foot of Mount Sorrow, to the right of Angel Glacier. Ford the creek and work up scree and stunted firs to the foot of the cliff. The upper corner is the biggest corner system on the wall and is easily seen from the parking lot (a second large corner just to its left is not the route). Begin on the ramp that angles up and right toward the main corner system.
targets.name: Long Forgotten

targets.approach: Drive the Mount Edith Cavell road, which leaves the Icefields Parkway south of Jasper, to its end at the parking lot. Dune Wall is a conspicuous rock buttress at the foot of Mount Sorrow, to the right of Angel Glacier. Ford the creek and work up scree and stunted firs to the foot of the cliff. Spiceworms starts in the same spot as Stilgars Corner, and its anchors can be seen from the ground.
targets.name: Spiceworms

targets.approach: Drive the Mount Edith Cavell road, which leaves the Icefields Parkway south of Jasper, to its end at the parking lot. Dune Wall is a conspicuous rock buttress at the foot of Mount Sorrow, to the right of Angel Glacier. Ford the creek and work up scree and stunted firs to the foot of the cliff. Stilgars Corner is on the far right side of the wall and defines that sector.
targets.descent_text: Rappel from the bolted belay stations, which have rings.
targets.name: Stilgars Corner

targets.approach: Park at the large pullout with an outhouse on Highway 16 northeast of Jasper, toward Hinton. The trail starts at the far end of the pullout from the outhouse: skirt the pond, climb the steep hill, and continue up and left along the obvious trail, bearing left at forks, past a ladder to the cliffs. First Wall is the first sector, on the left a minute or two beyond the ladder. Lower Ramp is at the far left of the wall, up the prominent gully and ramp that has a tree at its base.
targets.descent_text: Walk off to climber's right of the wall, or rappel from the sport and trad anchors to the base.
targets.name: Lower Ramp

targets.approach: Take the trail from Moraine Lake to Sentinel Pass. Grand Sentinel stands beyond the pass toward Paradise Valley and is visible to the south from the trail. Descend from the pass by the hiker's path down the right side of the valley rather than the talus on the left (the Sentinel side), which is exposed to rockfall and slides. It lies on the tower's south side.
targets.name: South Face

targets.approach: Take the trail from Moraine Lake to Sentinel Pass. Grand Sentinel stands beyond the pass toward Paradise Valley and is visible to the south from the trail. Descend from the pass by the hiker's path down the right side of the valley rather than the talus on the left (the Sentinel side), which is exposed to rockfall and slides. The route lies around to the right of Cardiac on the tower.
targets.name: Syd and Nancy in Paradise

targets.approach: Start from the Devil's Gap trailhead in the Lake Minnewanka valley and follow the steep trail up to the base of Grey Ghost Wall, a south-facing wall.
targets.name: Bonanza

targets.approach: Walk up Cougar Creek past the Cosmology crag until an island of trees sits in the creek bed. Look left for an obvious cairn and follow the trail as it winds up the hillside. The trail soon meets a first step of rock, climbed at easy fifth class, then meanders over rock, scree and dirt below a significant cliff. Descend along the cliff base for a short distance to a right-facing crack, which is the start of the first technical section. A few pieces of gear in the crack gain the ridge, with a small tree to belay from.
targets.descent_text: After joining the Lady Macdonald scramble on the summit ridge, follow the hiker's scramble trail down to where Cougar Creek begins.
targets.name: East South East Ridge

targets.approach: From Jasper take Maligne Lake Road past the north end of Medicine Lake to a small paved pullout on the right, the fourth beyond the big pullout at the lake's north end (stop before a rockslide warning sign). A rocky drainage lies a short way south of the pullout. Follow it uphill as it narrows to a creek bed, keeping left of the creek, then continue up its gravel bed until it narrows again and stay on the ridge left of the deepening gully. Climb the steep slope to treeline, exit the trees angling right back to the edge of the gully, and head for a lone small tree where the scrambling begins. Scramble the broad buttress beside the gully, then switchback across the gully on ledges or climb a crumbly fourth-class corner, to arrive on the last slope under the wall. Move rightward beneath the wall, over a wooded rise, up a large sloping ledge to the final tree on it; the line begins right beside that tree.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the route; traverse back across the big ledge to reach the anchors for the first two pitches.
targets.name: The Nutcracker Ball (aka Clark's Corner)

targets.approach: From the Smith-Dorrien highway south of Canmore, park at the West Wind Pass trailhead and hike the good trail to the pass, from where the east face of the Rimwall is in view. Go left along the base of the wall to reach the routes. Canary in the Coal Mine takes the obvious line on the north face, past Candle in the Wind, and starts up slab.
targets.name: Canary in the Coal Mine

targets.approach: From the Smith-Dorrien highway south of Canmore, park at the West Wind Pass trailhead and hike the good trail to the pass, from where the east face of the Rimwall is in view. Go left along the base of the wall to reach the routes. From the pass, hike along the base of the Rim Wall to the first obvious right-facing corner and scramble up to the base of the crack.
targets.name: Pinko

targets.approach: From the Smith-Dorrien highway south of Canmore, park at the West Wind Pass trailhead and hike the good trail to the pass, from where the east face of the Rimwall is in view. Go left along the base of the wall to reach the routes. The Hobbit is on the left side of the wall.
targets.name: The Hobbit

targets.approach: Park at the gravel pullout near the northern edge of Jasper National Park, on the Hinton side, and follow the short gravel road toward the peak. Pass the cliff band on the left and take the trail up the northwest ridge. When the trail splits left toward the scramble route, stay with the edge of the forest on the ridge up to the steeper ground. A stretch of scrambling follows; head for the obvious left-leaning ramp and chimney feature on the northwest face. The climb starts at a two-bolt belay anchor.
targets.descent_text: Rappel from the Metolius rap hangers on the route, or scramble up to the summit and follow the scramble route down.
targets.name: Chimney Route

targets.approach: The Ship's Prow is the large prominent feature attached to Mount Grassi above Canmore. From Canmore follow the Nordic Centre signs, then continue on Three Sisters Drive into the Homesteads area and on to Wilson Way, parking next to the boulder-edged stormwater channel. Follow the channel upstream, pass through the gap in the wooden barrier, and take the old road east, crossing the dry streambed that drains the bowl below the northwest face. Turn right onto the road along the east side of the streambed, bearing right at the fork, to a little cliff terminating a rocky spur. From there either continue east along the road to the base of the northeast ridge and climb its open east side to the prow, or drop into the west drainage, which is overgrown at first but opens to a bowl below the northwest face. Broadside is on the upper left part of the northwest face: it begins on a crack line slanting up to the right, far to the right of the pair of prominent corners and finishes in the subcorner and crack system between them.
targets.name: Broadside

targets.approach: The Ship's Prow is the large prominent feature attached to Mount Grassi above Canmore. From Canmore follow the Nordic Centre signs, then continue on Three Sisters Drive into the Homesteads area and on to Wilson Way, parking next to the boulder-edged stormwater channel. Follow the channel upstream, pass through the gap in the wooden barrier, and take the old road east, crossing the dry streambed that drains the bowl below the northwest face. Turn right onto the road along the east side of the streambed, bearing right at the fork, to a little cliff terminating a rocky spur. From there either continue east along the road to the base of the northeast ridge and climb its open east side to the prow, or drop into the west drainage, which is overgrown at first but opens to a bowl below the northwest face. Reach the face, then traverse toward the short far end of the face to the obvious right-facing corner where Scurvy starts.
targets.name: Scurvy

targets.approach: The Ship's Prow is the large prominent feature attached to Mount Grassi above Canmore. From Canmore follow the Nordic Centre signs, then continue on Three Sisters Drive into the Homesteads area and on to Wilson Way, parking next to the boulder-edged stormwater channel. Follow the channel upstream, pass through the gap in the wooden barrier, and take the old road east, crossing the dry streambed that drains the bowl below the northwest face. Turn right onto the road along the east side of the streambed, bearing right at the fork, to a little cliff terminating a rocky spur. From there either continue east along the road to the base of the northeast ridge and climb its open east side to the prow, or drop into the west drainage, which is overgrown at first but opens to a bowl below the northwest face. The route climbs the prow itself. The start is a good distance left of the prow itself, under a broad water-worn scoop, with some scrambling before the first belay.
targets.name: Ship's Prow

targets.approach: The slab is reached from a pullout on the westbound Trans-Canada Highway, roughly midway between the Mount Norquay turnoff and the Bow Valley Parkway turnoff. Cross the animal fence at the runoff channel and follow the channel a short way, then climb the ridge on its right under the power lines and through burned timber, picking up a faint trail to the crest. Follow the crest past flat spots and rock steps; where the ridge dips to a col and then steepens, take the trail round to the right and onto the ridge again. A slab blocks the ridge at the next flat spot, so drop down and left past a cairn, cross a stand of trees and a wide scree-filled gully, staying left of it (ignore the trail that heads up to a rock step). Follow the downhill trail to the edge of a cliff, which is the top of the lower slab, turn right along it to an opening, and the upper slab lies straight ahead. The route climbs the corner immediately to the right of Escargot Corner.
targets.name: Calamari Crack

targets.approach: Park at the roadside on the Icefields Parkway a few hundred metres south of the Weeping Wall, beside a collection of large boulders. Vacation Wall is the main multi-pitch wall behind the boulder: continue up past the boulder to reach it. The route climbs the rock directly behind the line called El Penata Clamor.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the route from its bolted belays.
targets.name: Limestone Vacation

targets.approach: South of Jasper, take the Icefields Parkway side road (Highway 93A) past Athabasca Falls to Leech Lake and park at the pullout. A maintained trail leads into the forest to the Lost Boys crag. Wasted Youth Wall is the sector right of the Main Wall. Bloodline follows the obvious big flake with a wide crack at the right end of the Main Wall, marked at its base with painted letters and a number in yellow.
targets.name: Bloodline
